problems.summary: Six Arch errors drove the whole cost of this issue, and five were failures to verify something checkable in one command. The implementation was byte-identical from round 0 and both reviewers approved its substance; four correction rounds went to records, three of the four final-round corrections traced to Arch's own text, and two agent turns were spent on a fabricated premise and an execution limit.
problems.evidence: (1) Promoted review B's INFERENCE (CALC_SURF_DR writes hFac_surfC, so the guard uses the reference thickness) into the round-2 design as a required record without checking the call chain; update_surf_dr.F:56/:92 install it into hFacC one call later and forward_step.F:484 calls UPDATE_SURF_DR in exactly that branch. Review A refuted it by grepping every writer. (2) Cited a lag route inside IF (doResetHFactors), which defaults to .FALSE. at set_defaults.F:185. (3) Claimed doResetHFactors is set by neither experiment; it is .TRUE. at cs32/input.seaice/data:31 and input.in_p/data:42. (4) Told bob that final_verification.py check passes under --owner bob, having never run that command; TRUE_EXIT was 1. (5) Handed bob a pgrep -f preflight that self-matches - a trap I had hit and fixed earlier the same session. (6) Handed bob a 110-minute suite for a context that lives ~59 minutes, having run the same suite myself in a long-lived session.

problems.summary: An externally killed verification run is recorded permanently as a scientific failure of the candidate, with stable true, because interruption() recognises signal death only through a negative return code.
problems.evidence: RUNOFF-040's first final attempt ran 3542.95 s over 36 of 59 commands and was terminated by a process-group SIGTERM, which surfaced as a POSITIVE 124 from the intermediate shell. interruption() (verify.py:47-55) returned None, stable stayed true, and the wrapper printed 'verification failed (exit 124)' - against a candidate two reviewers had approved. Zero FAIL tokens in 249970 bytes of log; 35 of 36 started commands passed. The authoritative witness was already in the text: execute()'s own handler wrote 'verification received signal 15' as the last line.

problems.summary: A note carried from RUNOFF-030 on the stated ground that it hid no live false claim produced one. The footprint sweep does not scan .py, so a stale assertion count survived in a test while its twins in .md files were caught and corrected by the sweep.
problems.evidence: Review B measured tests/rnf/refusal_check.py:1530 still reading 'The four "which bounds applied" lines of RNF_SUMMARY' after this issue added a fifth, contradicted by the file's own comment three lines below, while docs/code_map.md:50 and pkg/rnf/README.md:136 were both caught. Review B had also measured in RUNOFF-030 that 41 footprint candidates sit in .py prose, 23 of them the sweep's own fixtures.

problems.summary: A shell one-liner Arch supplied was unexecutable by the role it was given to, and the role had to substitute a sanctioned pattern and say so.
problems.evidence: The detached-launch command needed setsid, nohup, &, cd and two '> file' redirects, none of which bob's permission envelope allows. It used a Write-then-python launcher whose subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True) calls setsid(2) and opens the output files from inside the program, achieving the same semantics and the same paths, and flagged the substitution rather than improvising silently - warning that another role with Write would hit the same wall.

solutions.reference: this retrospective and the LL entry it proposes
solutions.reason: Not mechanisable as a tool change, so recorded as the discipline it is: when relaying a reviewer finding, separate the MEASUREMENT (which can be passed on) from the INFERENCE (which must be verified before it becomes a requirement), and never state that a gate passed without running it. All six instances share one shape - a claim stated more broadly than it was checked - and each was refutable by a single command. The asymmetry worth recording is that a coordinator's unverified claim is more expensive than an implementer's, because it enters the record as a requirement and is then faithfully implemented.

The PROCESS failure is fixed and the remaining work is a tracked project defect, so this is deliberately not filed against the process ledger. What failed was that RUNOFF-030 carried this note on an explicit, checkable ground - that the gap hid no live false claim - and nothing ever re-checked that ground; it expired silently and a reviewer found the instance. The response was to promote the note to RUNOFF-042 rather than renew it, which is the practice this records: when a carry rests on a stated condition, the condition is itself the thing to re-measure, and a carry whose ground has expired is an issue rather than a note. The sweep's .py blindness is NOT fixed and is not claimed to be; RUNOFF-042 owns it with acceptance criteria and the demonstrate-it-failing requirement.

Deferred against that issue because the two share a root in how long-running verification is launched and classified, and fixing the launch path is the natural place to settle what a role can execute. The immediate mitigation needs no code: Arch should supply long-run launches in the Write-then-Popen(start_new_session=True) form that bob demonstrated, rather than a shell one-liner, since that form is executable by the roles that need it and achieves identical detachment semantics.

confirmations.summary: The implementer refused to work around a premise Arch had fabricated, and reported the contradiction instead of absorbing it.
confirmations.evidence: Told that final_verification.py check passes under owner bob, it ran the command, got exit 1, and reported that the dispatch message was wrong rather than quietly re-navigating or patching the packet. It also declined to clear the stale arch orientation, correctly reasoning that it was the arch role's receipt, that the tool's remedy ends in a fresh footer only arch can produce, and that recovery.md forbids an agent editing a stored receipt.

confirmations.summary: The implementer refused to present an exit-124 failure record as a qualification receipt, and gave four independent facts that the termination was external.
confirmations.evidence: 'There is no receipt and no scientific evidence reference to report... what exists is a failed-execution record, which is a different thing and I will not present it as a receipt.' It then cited the SIGTERM handler's own log line, its trailing echo never running, the per-command timeout never being approached in a 3543 s run, and zero FAIL tokens across 35 completed commands - and found the interruption() classifier defect behind the mislabelling.

confirmations.summary: Asked to check rather than concede or defend its own refuted inference, review B grepped, agreed without reservation, named its own failure precisely, argued AGAINST its own interest on severity, and supplied a replacement better than deletion.
confirmations.evidence: 'I stopped at the routine named in the warning instead of grepping the writers, which is exactly the check the other reviewer did.' It agreed the item deserved must_fix rather than note status because the record would invite multiplying in a factor already inside hFacC, then supplied the real asymmetry running the opposite way: surf_dr clamps to Rmin_surf and continues while r* refuses to continue. Review A verified that replacement at the computing lines and judged it better than deletion, since the deleted leg answered a question maintainers genuinely ask.

confirmations.summary: Asked to read its own replacement text as a reviewer rather than its author, review B found the overclaim in its own sentence, agreed with the other reviewer against itself, and still argued for carrying it rather than spending a round.
confirmations.evidence: It verified calc_r_star.F:201 and :241-242 and concluded that 'unbounded in the r* one' is right read as 'not clipped' and wrong read as 'can fall arbitrarily far', since CALC_R_STAR stops the run. It then drew the note-versus-must_fix line on consequence: round 2's defect invited a wrong number applied silently to every enforced limit on an r* grid, while this one invites dead code - and supplied exact replacement wording plus the single condition that would upgrade it.

confirmations.summary: The implementer diagnosed why its own original claim was false rather than just correcting it, and the diagnosis generalised to a habit shared with Arch.
confirmations.evidence: Its 'only run-time writer of hFacC' claim came from a grep piped through head -12, which silently truncated an alphabetically ordered list immediately after update_r_star.F. Its first retry failed the opposite way by excluding h0FacC and hFac_surf anywhere on the line, which removes the real writers because those names sit on the right. Two grep shapes, two wrong answers, from one habit of trusting a filtered pipeline - the same habit that let Arch push a commit over a failing structural suite through tail, and that bob then caught in itself a third time on a piped check invocation.

confirmations.summary: The implementer built the witness from its description and confirmed it on the pre-change build BEFORE adding the check, which is what makes the refusal meaningful rather than circular.
confirmations.evidence: On the committed RUNOFF-030 build: exit 0, normal end, zero EXF WARNING lines, one non-zero cell at 1.2852284e-03 m/s, RNF_INIT_VARIA flux sums both 4.0e7. Its control at twice the bound per source was refused in RNF_NC_READ_FLUX, showing the per-source guard was live in exactly that file shape and only the aggregate escaped.

confirmations.summary: Launching a run longer than an agent turn under its own session leader works, and is now demonstrated end to end.
confirmations.evidence: PID 2945572 with sid = pgid = pid, verified from /proc rather than assumed, survived the turn boundary that killed the previous attempt at 3543 s and completed the full 59-command suite in 6602.3 s with exit 0 and zero FAIL tokens. Today's loop-hold fix detected it correctly as {'script': 'tools/esx/final_verification.py'}, so the iteration was held rather than spent - the first live validation of that fix in the case it was built for.

carry_forward: TWO ESX-team issues remain Proposed and are the owner's next instruction: TEAM-FOOTER-ORIENTATION-FRESHNESS-001 (the capture-gate asymmetry, including that an implementer footer citing a superseded sealed report passes BOTH gates because validate's identity check needs an expected_report only a reviewer packet supplies, and that footer_contract.py:84 skips the deep checks on a REJECT) and TEAM-VERIFY-SIGNAL-MISCLASSIFIED-001.

Review B's carried note on its own wording: 'unbounded in the r* one' at RNF.h:527-529 and docs/package_design.md:761-764 should become 'nothing clamps - CALC_R_STAR stops the run instead', with exact replacement text in its footer. It upgrades to a must_fix if the 'where 0.2 comes from' paragraph is ever moved or trimmed, so attach the note to both paragraphs.

Review B's carried note on the fork: the removed ESX record is gone from the tree and nets out of master..new_runoff, but b36247c18 is still in the branch's commit HISTORY, so a reviewer browsing the PR commit-by-commit sees a commit adding an ESX review note. The project's contribution rules do not mention squashing. An owner decision before the PR, which needs owner approval anyway.

Five carried notes on the guard itself, none a defect today: the NaN arm is unreachable on a supported input and its validity rests on the optfile (-O0 with no fast-math measured; -ffinite-math-only would void it and the pre-existing rnf_init_fixed.F:728-737 tests alike); neither enrolled case separates RNF_cellVolMax from any value within 1 per cent of it, so a sub-1% tightening mutant passes both; the GLOBAL_SUM_INT is unconditional for every useRNF run and unmeasured beyond 2 processes; RNF_tgtK is fixed at init while the guard re-evaluates kSurfC each step, which could diverge under pkg/shelfice remeshing via shelfice_remesh_c_mask.F:226-227; and review A's caveat that the ~200 km Amazon mouth argument is thin on the narrowest reading (~50 km north channel, ~25 cells, below the 32 needed).

Unmeasured regimes this issue documents but cannot execute: nonlinFreeSurf > 0 with select_rStar = 0 (no experiment here runs it, so both the floor claim and the clamp-versus-stop contrast are source readings), the r* pass-then-refuse drift (stated from code and the measured live range, never demonstrated by an executed mid-run flip), the one-step lag (read from the forward_step call structure, not instrumented), and any 2 km configuration (arithmetic on a stated grid; none exists in verification/).

No adjoint evidence for the new guard. It adds an integer GLOBAL_SUM_INT and a conditional STOP to a routine TAF differentiates; integers are not active and PRINT_ERROR/STOP are not differentiated, so the implementer judged it TAF-safe by inspection, but no adjoint test was run. RUNOFF-017 territory.

DECIDE rather than carry a fourth time: tests/footprint_claim_sweep.py is enrolled in no configured suite, so its three guards and its self-test run only when someone invokes the procedure. Both RUNOFF-030 reviewers raised it and both deferred to Arch; RUNOFF-042 says to settle it there. Enrolling --self-test alone (exit 4, no triage noise) is one line in esx/project.json.
